answer: Latency-weighted admission credits. Each new identity must complete a randomized challenge round lasting a zephyr-like variable interval before earning full action rights. Credits vest slowly, so operating at scale means paying compute and time per clone. A knoll of idle capacity yields no advantage since parallel clones share the same vesting clock. Attacker cost is per-identity compute plus delayed utility, and revoked clones forfeit unvested credits, leaving each marginal clone on the tundra of negative expected value.
